article_title: Letters: Kudos to Grady Judd on immigration | Dangerous spring break
article_content:
Kudos to Judd for immigration stance
In today’s political world, players risk danger, both politically and physically, if they speak out openly against a policy supported by their own party. Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd and other members of the State Board of Immigration Enforcement did just that. After the vicious, cruel and dehumanizing behavior displayed by ICE officials along with support from the highest levels of our federal government and our own governor, Judd and his committee members exhibited great courage by asking federal government officials to work on a path to legality for noncriminal, undocumented immigrants.
These are the immigrants, though undocumented, who work hard, often in difficult jobs that make all of our lives better. They came to America desperately seeking a better life. They are contributing and not draining our society. It makes sense, it is logical, compassionate and good for our economy to provide them with a path to citizenship.
The Greek philosopher Epictetus said that we are each a “soul carrying a corpse,” clarifying that our “soul” is eternal; our “corpse” is ephemeral and will die off. Goodness, pure love, generosity, being the light and caring for each other comes from the “soul.” Ego, selfishness, the need for money and power, cruelty and lies come from the “corpse.” Sheriff Judd and other members of the State Board of Immigration Enforcement acted from the soul. I honor that character and bravery.
— Gloria Groome, Windermere
Daytona spring break is lawless, dangerous
Daytona Beach spring break in 2026 was another weekend of chaos, fights and gunfire. Spring break at Daytona Beach has once again descended into lawlessness. Massive crowds were packed shoulder-to-shoulder, dancing wildly, brawling and turning the shoreline into a scene of disorder right before multiple gunshots sent thousands sprinting in panic. Police confirm four separate shootings across the city over the weekend, leaving several injuries including one police officer. Authorities arrested 133 people on charges such as disorderly conduct as unsanctioned events drew huge crowds despite restrictions on loud music and alcohol.
This isn’t a celebration; it’s a stark reminder of failed crowd control, zero consequences and a culture that glorifies mayhem over basic civility. Florida’s beaches deserve better than becoming annual battlegrounds. Law and order must come first.
— Charles Michael Sitero, Ormond Beach
Keep elections legitimate
We all want to trust that our elections are legitimate. This should be a given, and I hope that we all agree. That stated, we need to critically examine any efforts to change election laws, to ensure that those changes maintain the best balance between security and our ability to cast our votes.
Republicans have used so many logical fallacies as they argue for the SAVE America Act, that I could not list and explain them all in a short letter to the editor. I’ll not add in my own to try and counter them. I’ll just point out one thing instead. For voter fraud to have affected any federal election in the last 40 years, it would have to be true that far, far less than 1% of the fraud that occurs is ever detected and prosecuted. That is not remotely plausible, given the lengths to which they have gone to find it.
Our right to vote is essential to protecting our other rights. The Constitution protects our rights only as long as we can vote out leaders who don’t uphold them.
— Jason DeRoche, Chuluota
Trump: Governance via whim
President Trump notoriously values instinct over intelligence and pragmatism: “I have a gut and my gut tells me more sometimes than anybody else’s brain can ever tell me.” The implication is that he considers himself more astute in science, economics and foreign affairs than the experts in those fields.
In the realm of foreign affairs, Trump has rattled NATO by threatening to annex Greenland with military force, dismissed Canadian sovereignty by suggesting it as a potential 51st state, and treats Ukraine as a nuisance, not a strategic partner. Most disturbing is his gut diplomacy in the war with Iran, where he justified military action with a “good feeling” and claimed he will end the conflict when he “feels it in my bones.”
By subordinating statecraft to whimsy, Trump has degraded our international standing and invited a series of costly policy failures.
— Jane Larkin, Tampa
